label: Retry and failure policy
gloss: when a step fails, try again a few times; if it still fails, park the record where someone will see it
why: A flow that works on a clean day still meets a rotated token or a slow server. Retries give a transient failure a second chance; the failure policy says what happens if it never recovers. Skip drops the record silently. Dead-letter parks it and alerts an owner. At Beacon, the PO Register rejects the connection once on Day 3; with retries the lookup recovers, and with dead-letter nothing can vanish unnoticed.
cue: a failure nobody sees is the worst outcome; a retry count and a dead-letter are the two settings that stop it

failures.message: the PO register rejected the connection token (it was rotated overnight)

task: The PO Register rejects the first call today. Set the flow so the lookup recovers on a retry, and so a record that never recovers is parked in dead-letter with an alert instead of being dropped.
notes: Retries: how many extra attempts a failing step gets before the flow gives up (1 to 5 is sane).
On failure - skip: the record is dropped and nobody is told.
On failure - dead-letter: the record is parked in dead-letter and the on-call owner is alerted.
On failure - retry-forever: the run hangs until someone notices.

checks.label: The flow succeeds despite the failed first call
The PO lookup recovered on a retry
